topic: Spot the signs of anchoring bias when you shop or negotiate prices

script.title: Anchoring bias in pricing: why first numbers trap you
script.hook: Why does the first price you see trap you?

scenes.text: Why does the first price you see trap you?

motion_action.headline: Why does the first price you see trap

scenes.text: Retailers set a high sticker, then slash it dramatically.
Your brain latches onto that initial number, anchoring your judgment.
Research suggests offers close to the anchor feel fair.
When negotiating, drop the first figure and watch resistance rise.
If the seller starts low, you’ll likely settle higher than needed.
A simple trick: mentally reset to zero before any price talk.
Now you know the real reason:

script.loop_transition_text: Now you know the real reason:
script.description:
Anchoring bias tricks you into overpaying when you shop or negotiate.
Learn the subtle signs and how to reset your mind.
Spot the cue and avoid costly decisions.
